_comment: Navigation sweep profile for Super Mario Bros. (ADR-0239, PRD F14.16).
Read by scripts/record_navigation_sweep.py.
READ THIS FIRST - WHAT THE LIBRARY'S FILE ACTUALLY IS. The ROM at
<library>/Super Mario Bros. (1985) (Nintendo).nes is NOT retail Super
Mario Bros. Its own title screen reads 'SUPER MARIO BROS. / REVISITED'
over the menu 'ONE PLUMBER / TWO PLUMBERS / TOP- 000000' where the retail
ROM reads '1 PLAYER GAME / 2 PLAYER GAME'; the screenshot is
runs/f1417/smb1/probe/title/mesen-home/Screenshots/smb1_000.png
(captured 2026-09-26, frame 300). scripts/stages/smb3/stage-set.json had
already recorded the same finding from the other side ('the old library's
SMB1 file is a hack under a misleading name'). Every copy of an SMB1-named
ROM on this machine is that one file: whole-file SHA1
155C2E0936E8B4A44950195B81A94257F42D5D93, No-Intro payload SHA1
B606D2CF1EC5E8732B8748D272417B7FECB4EEF7 (the five paths checked are
listed in runs/f1417/smb1/RESULT.md). Every figure this profile produces is
a figure for THAT file and for nothing else, which is why romSha1 above
pins it: a later session handed a retail dump must not inherit them, and a
reader comparing these numbers with a community pack for retail SMB1 would
be comparing two different games.
WHAT STILL HOLDS ANYWAY, and why the sweep is still run. The hack is built
on the retail engine, and the published RAM map's bytes were measured, not
assumed, on this dump: pinning $075F at 0x00-0x07 makes the game load a
different level for each value (eight distinct level-layout addresses,
below), and the HUD's own world digits read 1-1 through 8-1. So the
selector is real, the citation is real, and the coverage figures are a real
measurement of a real ROM - of this one.
RUNG. ADR-0239 s1's second: a published RAM selector, pinned for the run.
Rung 1 does not exist on this game - there is no stage select, no password
and no continue code that picks a place, only the warp zones, which are
reached by playing. Rung 3 (a save state reached by search, chain or movie)
is out of this slice's scope.
SELECTOR AND VALUES. $075F is the current world and $0760 the level inside
it (DataCrystal, 'Super Mario Bros./RAM map': '0x075F World', '0x0760
Level'). The byte is 0-based - pinning 0x00 lands on World 1-1 and 0x07 on
World 8-1 - and the level byte is 0 by the game's own boot, so the world
pin alone puts a session on that world's FIRST level. That was measured
rather than assumed, and it is the one thing this game's world select can
be asked for without a second address: pinning $0760 as well would buy
1-2, 1-3 and 1-4, and the published map does name it, but the sweep's
subject is the place a selector reaches and this one reaches eight of
them from one address.
MEASURED ON THIS DUMP, 2026-09-26, one 40 s session per value from
power-on with the pin in place and no input past the title: $00E7, the
level layout address the game computed for the level it loaded, reads 90,
CF, 1B, 39, 3D, 5D, 80, 01 for values 00-07 - EIGHT DISTINCT ADDRESSES,
which is what each value's ramCheck asserts. The screenshots agree: the
HUD's world digits read 1-1 through 8-1 (a stacked crop of all eight is
runs/f1417/smb1/probe/hud-stack.png).
AND THE ADDRESSES ARE REAL LEVEL DATA, checked against the ROM itself,
which is the strongest evidence here and the reason a reader can trust a
first screen that looks the same on five worlds. $00E7 is a pointer into
the ROM's level data; resolving the eight addresses to file offsets in the
same PRG bank and reading them back shows that the five values 01, 02, 03,
05 and 06 land on a byte stream that begins 0F 20 4E 42 6E 40, and that
this six-byte prefix occurs EXACTLY FIVE TIMES in the whole 40 KB ROM -
the five offsets are the only five. So worlds 2, 3, 4, 6 and 7 genuinely
share the opening objects of their first level, and the identical castle
at the left of those five sessions' screenshots is the ROM's own data and
not a warp that failed. Values 00, 04 and 07 land elsewhere and draw
something else. The command and its output are in runs/f1417/smb1/RESULT.md.
WHY THIS IS NOT THE ATTRACT DEMO. A run that never took the select records
the demo under the value's name, and the F12.10 report already has a
column for exactly that (#409). $0770 is the game mode and reads 01
('Start normal', the map's own list) in the final state of all eight 40 s
sessions, so every one of them is a game and not the demo; it reads 00
('Start demo') only in sessions whose blind body has already lost three
lives and let the attract mode take the screen back.
NO LIVES PIN, so ADR-0239 s3's inert control does not apply. $075A is the
published lives counter and the body does lose lives - that is the point,
ADR-0184 s4 wants the deaths - but the counter is not pinned and no session
of this sweep is launched with a pin other than the selector. The blind
body is allowed to reach GAME OVER and the attract demo, and the sessions
that do are reported as such rather than hidden.
CAVEAT THAT APPLIES TO EVERY SESSION. A stage that is entered rather than
played never shows the stage-clear transition (ADR-0184's 2026-09-14
amendment): the selector is pinned for the whole run, so the game never
observes the world advancing. A session that DOES clear a level still
records that level's own end, but the world-to-world transition does not
exist in any pack here.

_ramCheckComment: Each value's ramCheck reads $00E7 - DataCrystal's 'Level layout address' -
off the session's final state. It is deliberately NOT the selector's own
address: a RAM cheat substitutes the byte on the CPU read bus and leaves
the byte in memory alone, so $075F reads 00 in the final state of a warped
run however far the pin went (measured on all eight values). $00E7 is the
game's own value with no pin on it, and it names the level the loader
actually took, which is what s4 asks a check to say.
The expected values are measured, not published, and a check is not a
cheat, so ADR-0184 s5's source rule does not reach them: what they say is
which of the ROM's level layouts the game resolved, and the ROM check
above is what makes them mean something.
Value 00 is included because ADR-0239 s6's subject is every place the
selector reaches and 0x00 is one of the eight. It is also the sweep's own
inertness control - the pin at the identity value, measured against a
baseline recorded with NO pin at all - and s4 scores it did-not-warp by
construction, because it records exactly what the baseline records. That
row is the control and not a failure, and the union is the same with or

navigation.source: DataCrystal, Super Mario Bros./RAM map (datacrystal.tcrf.net/wiki/Super_Mario_Bros./RAM_map, revision oldid=70369; the live page is behind a JS challenge, so it was read 2026-09-26 through the Wayback Machine snapshot http://web.archive.org/web/20260912171231/https://datacrystal.tcrf.net/wiki/Super_Mario_Bros./RAM_map): '$075F World' and '$0760 Level', and '$00E7 Level layout address'. Values 0x00-0x07 = Worlds 1-8, measured on this dump 2026-09-26 (the HUD's own world digits read 1-1 through 8-1). Published map, cited per ADR-0184 s5.

_defaultsComment: The entry is the game's own title path, run as input rather than as a
state: a navigation session starts from power-on with the pin already set,
and the boot's own level load is what the pin steers. No save state is
used, so nothing unversioned has to travel with this profile.
The body is a blind 360-frame rhythm - hold B and Right for 20 frames, hold
B, Right and A for 16 - repeated by record_navigation_sweep.py until the
120 s budget is covered, exactly as Contra's and SMB3's profiles do
(ADR-0184's amendment: effective input time, not the cheat, is what moves
the picture). It is not a route: it is what keeps a figure's cycle on the
screen, and a session it loses ends on the attract demo, which the report
The rhythm was picked by measurement, not by taste: three shapes were run
on World 3-1 at 120 s and read against the baseline of that moment (236
drawn keys) - 20/16 gave 81 new keys, 34/18 gave 65, 12/12 gave 56. The
losing arms are unversioned under runs/f1417/smb1/probe/bodyA and bodyB.
The baseline was re-recorded with the winning body afterwards and now reads
203 drawn keys; runs/f1417/smb1/RESULT.md carries the sweep's final numbers.
